title: Shanahan Reflects on 6-0 Start, Gritty Finish Over Commanders
headline: Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) is questionable after leaving early, Demarcus Robinson won't play this week, and Romello Height and Ashtyn Davis earned bigger roles in the win.
summary: Shanahan said Mike Evans's Achilles tendinitis, which had bothered him all week, flared up during the game and kept him out after the first half. He described it as soreness rather than something needing more testing, and said Evans felt confident enough to play but the coach knew he might not last. Shanahan was frustrated by three-and-outs and penalties that stalled the offense in the second half, while praising the defense for holding on despite losing Upton Stout and Luke Gifford. He said Romello Height had a big impact, and Ashtyn Davis stepped in at corner and played pivotal snaps in the fourth quarter. On Christian McCaffrey, he said the team used him in the slot and at receiver to mix up receiver options. He said Demarcus Robinson won't be ready this week, and that a Deebo Samuel return is possible around the bye week. He also said a receiver returning from a long injury is expected back soon and the team has enough depth for now. Shanahan closed by saying he was proud of the team's competitive stamina in finishing the 6-0 start.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 10/21/26
headline: Terry McLaurin is out for the season with a torn patellar tendon, and Dan Quinn expects Van Jefferson and other receivers to take on bigger roles.
summary: Quinn opened by saying captain Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon, will have surgery, and is out for the rest of the season, which he called a gut punch. He described the team's first six games as adversity-filled and said the reset and response are what he is focused on during the bye. Quinn praised the second half against San Francisco as much stronger than the first half and said getting the whole game in sync is the key. He said the offensive line performance fell below the standard he expects and that the staff will keep searching for the right interior combination. He said the bye will be used for a self-scout to streamline the playbook into a smaller set of things the team can execute, with tweaks rather than a new system. On defense, he wants better pre-snap communication and fewer explosive pass plays. On Jayden Daniels, he said the offense will be better when Daniels is fully back and expects more keepers and out-of-pocket plays off play action. He said injury updates on other players, including Javon and Treylon Burks, would come Monday after more imaging.

injuries.detail: Torn patellar tendon; will have surgery and is out for the rest of the season.

signals.claim: Will likely be elevated into a bigger role at receiver after McLaurin's injury, as he has already been once this season.
signals.note: With McLaurin out, Jefferson is a leading candidate to pick up targets and deep-threat snaps.

signals.claim: Expects Daniels to run more keepers and out-of-pocket plays off the play-action game as he develops.
signals.note: More designed runs and scramble opportunities would boost Daniels' rushing floor and fantasy ceiling.

topics.detail: Quinn said the line's performance was below the team's standard, especially in pass protection, and that he will keep trying combinations on the interior.
Quinn wants better pre-snap urgency and call communication and fewer explosive pass plays allowed, especially on first and second down.
Changes are expected to be smaller tweaks and streamlining rather than a new system or new plays, with a focus on being more decisive and precise.
Quinn said the team's plus-six turnover differential is not yet translating to wins and that the complementary football needs to be sharper.
